newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK MKTS UNIMPRESSED BY PREMIER'S POLICY SPEECH.
newsitem.headline: GREEK MKTS UNIMPRESSED BY PREMIER'S POLICY SPEECH.

text.p: Greek financial markets expressed scepticism at the newly-elected premier's policy speech on Thursday night saying it was too general and lacked boldness.

"The prime minister was not specific and I am not convinced that he knows what to do," said George Spelios, treasurer at private ErgoBank. "His speech sounded more like an academic lecture in a seminar and did not give me the impression of being delivered by someone in charge."
Spelios said he was interested in the 1997 budget but got no clue about it from Simitis' policy statements.
"We have seen a tight Italian budget and one would expect to see something similar from our side, but it looks to me as if nothing will be done," he added.

Newly-elected Prime Minister Costas Simitis vowed in parliament on Thursday night to fight tax evasion, cut spending, do away with tax breaks for the wealthy, speed up the implementation of public works and accelerate economic growth.
Other treasurers said that the premier's first major economic policy speech fell short of market expectations and he sounded more like a populist than a reformer.

"Simitis disappointed," said a treasurer at a foreign bank. "He has been portrayed by the media as a reformer and technocrat but he sounded to me more like a populist politician who leaves the initiative to others."

Other senior dealers agreed that the speech fell short of market expectations but Simitis would prove tougher than he sounded on the execution of stringent economic policy measures to honour his pledge and bring the country into the EMU by the year 2000.

"The statements were very general and surely disappointing, especially on the incomes policy front, but there is no way for Greece to join the EMU by 2000 as pledged by Simitis without adopting a tougher stance," said a bond dealer at a foreign bank. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
